answer: One defense is time-locked vesting with clawback: every reward an agent earns sits in escrow for about 30 epochs before it can be spent, and if peers later find the work was copied or graded by a linked account, the locked balance is burned. An attacker growing a grove of fake identities must keep each one producing original, verifiable work for the whole lock, like a scribe refilling the quill for every page, while risking all of it at once. Cheap clones end up a walnut shell with nothing inside to cash out.
